links.reason: The image is shared: பூவினுள் நாற்றம் நீ (Paripadal 3.63) and பூவினுள் நாற்றமும் போலுளன் (Tirumanthiram 2639). But Tirumular closes on எங்குங் கலந்துநின் றானே, which says the Lord is mingled in everything, and Paripadal says the same with அனைத்தின் உட்பொருளும் நீ. So the simile marker போல் does not set the god 'at one remove', and the theology the teaches sentence draws from it is not in the Tamil.

The echo is real. The idyll has பலர்புறங் கண்டவர் அருங்கலந் தரீஇப் புலவோர்க்குச் சுரக்கும் (71-72) and Akananuru 349 has அருங்குறும்பு எறிந்த பெருங்கல வெறுக்கை சூழாது சுரக்கும் நன்னன். Only சுரக்கும் and கலம் repeat, so the 'fixed two-line formula' claim is not shown. The note's முனைபாழ் (line 59) lies outside the printed span. The teaches sentence also never says what the akam poet does with the name, which is to set Nannan's giving against the husband who left.

Both turn on the end of the king's work: வேந்துவிடு விழுத்தொழில் எய்தி ... அரசுவிடுத்து (Ainkurunuru 466) and வேந்தன் வினையு முடிந்தன (Kar Narpathu 20). That is the stock mullai event of vinai mutittal. The contrast drawn between fact and inference is thin, because the friend also states the release as news. The teaches sentence ends on the shared situation itself.

links.reason: The two gestures are close but not the same. The Kural has ஒருகண் சிறக்கணித்தாள் போல நகும், a smile with one eye narrowed, while Kali 51 has கடைக் கண்ணால் கொல்வான் போல் நோக்கி, நகை கூட்டம் செய்தான், a killing side-glance and a smile. The observation that the sign of kurippu is given here by the man, and after her lie, is true. But Kali does not limit the Kural; it transfers the sign, so qualifies does not fit.

Both read omens of return: கண்ணும் ஆடும் ... வளையும் செறூஉம் (Ainkurunuru 218), and கனவும் ... இனிய, நல்இல் புள்ளும் பாங்கின (Akananuru 141). But Akananuru 141 also has the heart (நெஞ்சும் நனிபுகன்று), so 'from the house to the body' does not hold. Ainkurunuru 218 has no anxious friend at all, so the claim 'always ... against the friend's fear' fails. The pairing is largely the shared topic of omens.

The argument matches: அலந்த கிளைகள் அழிபசி தீர்க்கும் ... நீள்சுரம் போகி (Valayapathi 44) and நகுதல் ஆற்றார் நல்கூர்ந்தோர் (Akananuru 151). Against it the akam heroine sets அருள்பிறிது ஆபமன். But the fragment's context is unknown: its editor places it among verses that condemn wealth, and புன்கண்மை உண்டோ may be a question to be refuted. So the claim that its voice 'needs no answer' rests on an uncertain frame.

Kuruntokai 15 has நாலூர்க் கோசர் நன்மொழி போல வாயாகின்றே, the Kosar's word as the standard of truth. Akananuru 113 has பல்வேற் கோசர் who are நன்றுஅல் காலையும் நட்பின் கோடார் and of திரிபுஇல் சூழ்ச்சி. That is a real puram-name connection, and it shows the Kosar's fixed reputation for keeping faith. The teaches sentence holds, though 'war band's loyalty' slightly recasts Kuruntokai's sworn word.

The device is shared: a stag shading its fawn (மறிக்குநிழ லாகி, Kuruntokai 213) and a bull elephant bending a yaa tree for its mate (புன்தலை மடப்பிடி உணீஇயர் ... யாஅம் ஒற்றி, Akananuru 59). But in Akananuru 59 the image still serves the friend's comfort (thurai: வேறுபட்ட கிழத்திக்குத் தோழி சொல்லியது), and உள்ளார் is a separate complaint, so 'opposite ends' overstates. Two uses of one device are not incompatible claims, so tension does not fit.

The cane is shared: கரும்புபோல் கொல்லப் பயன்படும் கீழ் (Kural 1078) and கரும்பின்கோது ஆயினேம் யாம் (Thinaimozhi 39). In the Kural the cane is the base man, whose crushing is deserved; in the poem the refuse is the wife's drained beauty (நலம் உண்டான்). The Kural says nothing about waste, so 'the same image shows that what is crushed ... is left as waste' is the poem's point alone, dressed as the pair's. Qualifies does not fit.

The vocabulary echo is striking: துனி, புலவி and கனி appear in both. But in Kural 1306 கனி is over-ripe fruit, a failure, while in Thinaimalai 153 கனிகலவி is ripe union, so the words do not carry the same doctrine. The poem's sense is flagged uncertain: காணா எப்போதுமே கண் with நாணா may describe shy eyes in love, not a 'cost' of the quarrel. The teaches sentence builds on that uncertain reading.

Both decline to blame him for the wasting body: சொல்லின் எவனாம் தோழி (Kuruntokai 185) and கொடியர் எனக்கூறல் நொந்து (Kural 1236), and the contrast of loyalty with despair is defensible. But 'a man as unmoved as the rock' leans on reading the kaanthal over the rock (கன்மிசைக் கவியும்) as a figure of the man, which the Tamil does not fix. The marker itself names only one firm pair.

Kural 1225 names one enemy, மாலைக்குச் செய்த பகை. Thinaimalai 121 has ஒன்றல பல்பகை, a list (மடல்அன்றில், மாலை, படுவசி, ஆம்பல், கடல், கார்) that includes the same மாலை. The quatrain multiplies the single foe, a specific development carried by the shared word பகை. The teaches sentence holds, though ஆம்பல் and பொருத்தில் are uncertain.

The two poems are in one decade (பாணன் பத்து). In 471 the heroine says இன்னும் வருதி, 'you still keep coming'; in 477 the hero tells the bard உயவுத்துணை யாகச் சிறுவரைத் தங்குவை யாயின் காண்குவை ... எம் தேரே. Reading the two as one act seen from both sides is plausible, but 'turns out to be the man's own order' assumes a narrative link that separate decade poems do not state. The type is closer to develops than qualifies.

links.reason: Both urge giving now because of death. Purananuru 139 has கனிபதம் பார்க்கும் காலை யன்றே and சாதல் அஞ்சாய், and Naladiyar 5 has பின்னாவ தென்று பிடித்திரா ... கூற்றம். But the reasons differ: the Naladiyar's is the giver's own escape (கொடுத்தார் உயப்போவர்), while the bard's is the patron's likely death and his troupe's hardship (வருந்தலு முண்டு, என் பைதலங் கடும்பே). Calling them the same maxim overstates the match.

The exchange is the same and the valuation is opposite. Ainkurunuru 203 ranks கலிழி நீர் above தேன்மயங்கு பாலினும் இனிய, and Kuruntokai 356 pities the girl who refused அம்பொரிக் கலந்த பாலும் but must now gulp வெவ்வெங் கலுழி. These are incompatible judgements of the same trade of home's milk for the wild's mud, made by the friend and the foster mother. The teaches sentence is specific and true.

The echo யாம் செல்லும் ஆறே (Natrinai 9) and நாம் செல்லும் இடம் (Thinaimozhi 16), with the road drawn in bloom, is real. But neither poem states the girl's fear, and one pair does not establish a 'fixed speech'. The point about பாலை முரல is the venba's own and is not shown by the pairing.

Both join love-sickness and gossip: ஊரவர் கெளவை எருவாக (Kural 1147) and பெருகுமால் நம்அலர் (Thinaimalai 41). But the venba does not make the gossip a cause; heart and talk simply swell together, and பேண and பெருகா ஒருங்குவால் are uncertain. The pairing amounts to the shared topic of alar.

The campaign is plainly one: மோகூர் and the felled neem appear in both (வேம்புமுதல் தடிந்து, 44.15; விறல்வேம்பு அறுத்த, 49.16). But the teaches sentence's division is inexact. Song 49 also has the trophy, the neem, and 44 also has the battlefield (குராலம் பறந்தலை), so the songs overlap rather than divide the war.

The contrast is real: the onlookers' tiger-cub road with a heart உருமினும் கொடிதே (Natrinai 2) against the lover's நறுந் தண் பொழில கானம் (Natrinai 9). But Natrinai 9 is set in spring (மா நனை, குயில்), so the difference may be season and situation, and the two are not the same road. Different descriptions for different situations are not a tension, and 'danger ... is a judgment the voices make' does not follow.

The tortoise lore is shared and distinctive: யாமை இளம்பார்ப்புத் தாய்முகம் நோக்கி வளர்ந்திசின் (Ainkurunuru 44) and கடல் ஆமைதான் நினைக்க உருக்கொண்ட (Siddhar 176). But in the Sangam poem the young look at a mother who is present, and the point is presence (அதுவே ஐயநின் மார்பே). 'A model of care at a distance' therefore fits only the siddhar verse.

The phrase is shared: பிரிந்தோர்ப் புணர்ப்போர் (Kuruntokai 146) and பிரிந்தோர்ப் புணர்க்கும் (Kuruntokai 156). But the uniters of 146 also carry staffs and white headgear (தண்டுடைக் கையர் வெண்டலைச் சிதவலர்), so they may be of the Brahmin's own kind. And 156 ends open (மயலோ இதுவே), not in doubt of learning, so 'union was expected from social go-betweens, not from learning' is not in the Tamil.

The reply has the same shape: வல்வரவு வாழ்வார்க் குரை (Kural 1151) and ஒல்வார் உளரேல் உரையாய் (Thinaimalai 86). Each sends the message to whoever can survive it, and the venba adds the starving elephant of the road (பசியால்ஆள் பார்த்து மிசைந்தொழியும் அத்தம்). 'Stock reply' generalises from two verses, but the development is specific and true.

The two share a thurai (தோழி பருவங்காட்டி ... வற்புறுத்தியது) and the konrai, and their endings do differ: உவக்காண் தோன்றும் ... தேரன் against பசலை மருந்து. The claim that the venba 'has to stop at the season' because of its length is unsupported. A shared colophon situation with two endings is thin.

The heron is the one witness in both: குருகும் உண்டு தான் மணந்த ஞான்றே (Kuruntokai 25) and கொடுமை அறியாகொல் ... கண்டும் கானலுள் வாழும் குருகு (Ainthinai Ezhupathu 62). The venba turns the witness that saw nothing into one reproached for not knowing what it saw. The development is specific, though the venba's sense is flagged uncertain.

The bodily sign is the stock one: பணைத்தோள் ... நெகிழ (Ainkurunuru 318) and பணைநீங்கிப் பைந்தொடி சோரும் (Kural 1234). The poem's accusation, நசைநனி கொன்றோர், is real and absent from the couplet, so the teaches sentence holds. But the pairing rests on a sign every separation poem shares, and the note's gloss of பணைநீங்கி as 'broad shoulders' is loose (it is the loss of fullness).

The heroine's அருந்தவம் முயறல் ஆற்றாதேமே treats living apart (பிரிந்தும் வாழ்துமோ) as an ascetic's endurance, which matches the Kural's உற்றநோய் நோன்றல் ... தவத்திற் குரு. The teaches sentence is true and specific. But the poem applies the Kural's idea rather than limiting it, so qualifies does not fit.

Both name the Vicchi: விச்சியர் பெருமகன் with பாணர் and the uproar of குறும்பூர் (Kuruntokai 328), and the snub of the young Vicchi lord, பாடுநர்க்கு அடைத்த கதவின் (Purananuru 151). The bards' praise of his stand against the shut door is a real contrast. But whose door was shut is uncertain in 151, and nothing shows the akam poet knew of it, so 'despite his name for giving' is a generous reading.

Kural 1124 equates her with life: வாழ்தல் உயிர்க்கன்னள் ... சாதல் அதற்கன்னள். Kuruntokai 280 sets one day's union above the rest of life: ஒருநாள் புணரப் புணரின் அரைநாள் வாழ்க்கையும் வேண்டலென். Both measure the beloved against life itself, and the step from equation to trading life away is real and specific.

The patron's town is the vehicle for the wife in both. Natrinai 340 has வாணன் சிறுகுடி அன்ன என் கோள் நேர் எல் வளை, and Akananuru 204 has வாணன் சிறுகுடித் தண்டலை கமழும் கூந்தல. The teaches sentence holds: the returning husband and the wronged wife use the same puram place-name as the standard of her worth.

Kural 906 mocks men who fear their wives (இல்லாள் அமையார்தோள் அஞ்சு பவர் ... பாடிலரே), which is about subservience, not intimacy. Kural 1103 prizes sleep on a beloved's arms over the god's world. They share only shoulders and a heavenly comparison, and the teaches sentence, 'the books value the same intimacy in opposite ways', misreads 906.

The closing formula is the same: வானம் காண்தொறும் ... கண் (Ainthinai Ezhupathu 15) and வானம்காண் தோறும் துளிகலந்து வீழ்தருங் கண் (Ainthinai Aimpathu 5). The two bases of the likeness differ: drops falling with the rain, against காரோடு அலமரும் / நீரோடு அலமரும் tossing. The substance and motion split is slightly neat, since நீர் also appears, but the observation is true and specific.

The verbal echo காணுங்கால் (Kural 1286) and காணுங் காலே (Kuruntokai 252) anchors the pair. The Kural's woman cannot see fault in his presence, while the Kuruntokai woman names him கொடியன் and still will not blame him face to face (பழியாங் ஒல்பவோ). Love's blindness against chosen restraint is a true qualification.

The stances do differ: refusing any promise of return (வல்வரவு வாழ்வார்க் குரை, Kural 1151) against consent with a deadline (சென்மின் ... நீடாதல் ஓம்புமின், Natrinai 229). But they are two responses to a departure, not incompatible claims. Natrinai 229 also ends by pleading with the north wind already come (வாடையும் ... வந்து நின்றதுவே), which its colophon reads as holding him back.

The curse formula is exact: எம்போல் பெரு விதுப்புறுகமாதோ (Natrinai 293) and என்போற் பெருவிதுப்பு உறுக (Purananuru 291). It shows the eloped daughter mourned in a mourner's words. One detail is off: in Natrinai the curse falls on the youth's mother (காளையை ஈன்ற தாயே), not on 'the one who caused the loss' as in Purananuru, but the teaches sentence holds in substance.

Both set விருந்து against the king's war: வினைகலந்து வென்றீக வேந்தன் ... மாலை அயர்கம் விருந்து (Kural 1268) and வேந்தன் அருந்தொழில் தணியின் விருந்து நனி பெறுதலும் உரியள் (Ainkurunuru 442). The echo is real. But the teaches sentence turns on விருந்து as 'guests', when it may equally mean the new joy of reunion, so the 'whole household' reading is not fixed by the Tamil.

The bee as knower of scent is shared: கொங்குதேர் வாழ்க்கை ... நீயறியும் பூவே (Kuruntokai 2) and நாற்றம் இன்மையின் பசலை ஊதாய் (Natrinai 277). But Natrinai 277 ends with the plea என் நிலை உரையாய் சென்று, and the poem never says the appeal fails, so the 'limit of that office' is the note's inference.

The echo is close: நோய்க்குமருந் தாகிய பணைத்தோளோளே (Ainkurunuru 99) and தன்நோய்க்குத் தானே மருந்து (Kural 1102). But the poem does not state the Kural's paradox that the cause is the cure; it says only that she is the medicine. ஆகிய is an adjectival participle that need not fix a past time, so the teaches sentence's dating argument does not hold.

The two share Mal worshippers in crowds: உண்ணாப் பைஞ்ஞிலம் பனித்துறை மண்ணி (Patitruppattu 31) and மடையர், குடையர், புகையர், பூ ஏந்தி (Paripadal Thirattu 1). But மடையர் are bearers of food offerings, not a feasting crowd. The 'pleasure' is the simile of the town as துறக்கம், not the crowd's aim. The packet does not place the hymn at Koodal, and the lord of the hill is uncertain. 'Abstinence against festival' is built on these stretches.
links.text_issue: Paripadal Thirattu 1 lines 30-32 are obscure; line 44's numbering is off.

links.reason: The laughing sky is shared: நறுந்தண்கார் மெல்ல வினிய நகும் (Kar Narpathu 14) and வானம் நகுவதுபோல் மின்ஆட (Thinaimalai 122), heard as assurance by the friend and with despair by the heroine. That is a fair same-image point. But 'mockery' is not stated in 122, and two moods of one image are not incompatible claims.

வெருக்குப்பல் லுருவின் முல்லை (Kuruntokai 240) is a stock simile for the shape of the pointed buds, not a figure of menace. To read the wild cat's teeth as the waiting woman's predator view, against the returning man's முள்ளெயிறு ஏய்ப்ப (Kar Narpathu 21), stretches the simile.
links.text_issue: Kar Narpathu 21 colophon reads வினைமுற்றிய தலைமகள் for தலைமகன்.

links.reason: The counsel matches closely. Purananuru 35 has நின் விண்பொரு வியன்குடை வெயில்மறைக் கொண்டன்றோ? அன்றே; வருந்திய குடிமறைப் பதுவே, and the just sceptre bringing rain. Kalittokai 99 has அறன் நிழல் எனக் கொண்டாய், ஆய் குடை; அக் குடை புற நிழல் கீழ்ப் பட்டாளோ இவள்?, also with the rain of his செம்மை. The akam friend turns the puram standard of kingship on the husband, and the teaches sentence is true and specific.

Both refuse the straying husband: நண்ணேன் பரத்தநின் மார்பு (Kural 1311) and சென்றீ பெரும (Natrinai 360). The festival-doll image (விழவு ஒழி களத்த பாவை போல) does show use and discard, which differs from the Kural's ground that he is shared. But refusal at the door is the stock marutham situation, lines 6-11 are uncertain, and the primary speaker in the colophon is the friend.

Both kurinji poems set a hill tiger and its mate beside the velan's veri. Ainkurunuru 246 has பெண்பாற் புணர்ந்து மன்றில் பையுள் தீரும், and Natrinai 322 has ஊன் தின் பிணவின் உயங்கு பசி களைஇயர் ... புலி ஒடுங்கும். But Ainkurunuru 246 lines 2-4 are hard, and in Natrinai 322 the tiger belongs to the description of the man's land, not set against the rite. 'The partner and never the offering' is the note's generalisation.

poems.note: Lines 3-4 are hard to construe; the konrai bloom is a season sign, not an act.
The heron flock belongs to the Maranthai simile, which அன்ன joins openly to the hero's town.
The sea rising like a king's army (மன்கிளர்ந்த போலும்) echoes the kin rising (முன்கிளர்ந்து), but that is a single match.

vehicle: மனை அழுது ஒழிந்த புன் தலைச் சிறாஅர்

poems.note: Read as: the absent sea-going father is the delaying man, and the children's tears ended by the nungu are her grief ended by his coming; the scene could also be plain description of his village.

iraicchi.act: settles with the bees on the blossoming boughs, its loneliness ended (புலம்பு தீர்ந்து)
iraicchi.sense: In the spring even the bee is no longer alone, while the man stays away and she is.

poems.note: The bee scene is framed by the open simile அரும் தவம் ஆற்றியார் நுகர்ச்சி போல், so only the thumbi's act is taken as iraicchi.
Lines 2-4 are lost; the rule cannot be applied.
The bull is an open simile for the hero; the dog is part of the event, not a vehicle.

iraicchi.act: embraces its loved mate (அமர்துணை தழீஇ) and guards her against the tiger
iraicchi.sense: The man who sees the elephant protect its mate on his road will remember his own and return today.

poems.note: The parrot with the neem fruit is a visual simile (ஏய்க்கும்), with no act.
Line 2 is damaged; the bird that takes the thondri buds for fire cannot be given a sure sense.
The sky's ceasing and her tears drying are stated side by side, an open parallel.
Season description with no acting creature; the kodal-as-snake image is a simile of looks.
The flower similes (கோடல் போல், நீலம் போல்) are open; the tiger among elephants maps to nothing firm.

The bat that tires of neem fruit (முணைஇ) and craves the sweet iruppai matches the daughter leaving home for the lover, and its suffering in the dew (வைகு பனி உழந்த) matches her suffering on the road (அதர் உழந்து); the mother, as another speaker, may use it freely.
The parrots are a cause in the story (they brought her to guard the field), so striking them removes the sense.
The spilled milk is joined to her beauty by காஅங்கு, an open comparison.
Lines 1-3 are mostly lost; the rule cannot be applied.
The owl pair's hooting marks the dread of midnight; it is sound and mood, not an act bearing on the lovers.

iraicchi.act: returns from feeding on prawns and settles for the night on the punnai
iraicchi.sense: As the herons settle for the night, the man should stay the night with them and not leave.

poems.note: The paired sharks of line 7 mark the danger of the way back rather than an act of the lovers.
The bee is the addressee and messenger; the honeycomb is an open simile (போல).
The thurai text is garbled (தௌ¢விடை).

iraicchi.act: feigns drinking (கள்ளத்தின் ஊச்சும்) so that its doe may drink the little water of the pool
iraicchi.sense: A man whose road shows such care of a mate will think of her and come back.

poems.note: The kumizh flowers are joined to gold earrings by an open simile; the colophon reads தலைமகள் for தலைமகன்.

The hunter who ends his day's hunting and revels at home, forgetting his goods, matches the returning man whose work is done, hurrying to the joy of home; the vehicle is a person of the land, and the match may be read as plain scene-setting.
